mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the high inflation regime (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the 20-day return is positive despite the rate spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE change and SPX returns is < 0.3 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which lowers real interest rates through monetary policy lag and supports equity price appreciation over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the expansionary phase, or the effect is absent in non-cyclical periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy (HOUST) suggests supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty and pushing down equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during supply shocks, or the interaction term is not significant in regression.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months during a tightening cycle, it triggers a preemptive equity sell-off as investors anticipate future rate hikes, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month > 2% for 2 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS is rising
regime_hint: inflation above target in tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when the trigger occurs (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent outside the U.S. inflation target band.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in labor turnover (PAYEMS) below 5,000 monthly suggests reduced workforce instability, lowering hiring costs and improving firm profitability, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the low turnover period, or the effect is not robust to alternative labor metrics.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (implied via HOUST proxy) exceeding 5% in a month when industrial production is also rising suggests resilient consumer demand, which lowers real rates and drives equity price gains over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) despite the dual demand proxies, or the interaction is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of supply-side indicators (RSAFS / INDPRO) falls below 0.8 for two consecutive months, it indicates an imbalance favoring demand over supply, raising expectations of future price pressures and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when the imbalance persists (p > 0.05), or the effect is only observed in non-crisis periods.
